study.title: Message framing and purchase intention in an online experiment (illustrative example)
study.research_question: Does gain vs loss framing change purchase intention for a sustainable product, and does environmental involvement moderate it?
study.target_population: Adult online consumers who buy packaged consumer goods
study.estimand: Mean difference in purchase intention between gain-framed and loss-framed conditions, and how it differs between low and high environmental involvement.

constructs.name: Purchase intention
constructs.definition: Stated likelihood of buying the product

variables.label: Environmental involvement (mean of items)
variables.derivation: mean of 4 items, measured before the manipulation

sample_rules.frame: Panel respondents screened for buying packaged consumer goods

exclusion.rule: completion time under 40% of the pilot median

sample_rules.stopping_rule: Stop at 300 completed and valid responses per the sample-size plan; no interim looks at the outcome.

analysis_plan.hypothesis: H1: loss framing lowers purchase intention relative to gain framing
analysis_plan.model: Welch t-test / ANOVA on V_pi by V_cond

analysis_plan.hypothesis: H2: framing effect is larger at high environmental involvement
analysis_plan.model: Regression V_pi ~ V_cond * V_env with simple slopes at +/-1 SD

holdout_or_blinding.details: Experiment with preregistered analysis; no holdout needed.

governance.storage_and_retention: Export CSV from the platform; store on encrypted drive.

conditions: Pilot (n=30) completed; pilot data excluded from the main sample
